# Demo stage

Owner decision, 2026-10-31. This is the stage for the Meta Global AI
Developer Hackathon, Startup track. **Code is not ready.** This file is the
script and the rules check. It is not a live run, and it is not a submission.

## The demo

Three beats, in this order.

1. **Identity as an appliance.** The identity is the box: sealed methods, its
   own mount, a receipt for every call. It already exists. The demo uses it
   through that mount. It is not new work, and it is not rebuilt for the
   hackathon.
2. **Schema tag routing.** A request carries tags. Tags select controls.
   Controls select sealed operations. A tag that misses is a refusal, and the
   refusal names the rule. Muse Spark may suggest tags. The table decides.
3. **Drop-in CMS, generated from the system JSON.** Muse Spark writes a
   json-render spec from the sealed catalog. Fixed code validates that spec
   and renders it. The CMS is that spec. It is not a hand-built page.

Say the CMS **implements and evidences** the controls (redaction, audit,
access, retention, integrity). Do not say the product is certified.

## Off this demo

Team chat, the avatar script, on-chain anchoring, and moving an identity
between hosts. Older notes still describe them. They are not this stage.

## What exists, and what this stage must not show

| Beat | Present in the tree | Do not show as the product |
|---|---|---|
| Appliance | The identity, the mount, and call-file receipts exist. The hackathon mount still acts as the root session. The clone `etched::hackathon` is stopped and is not a sled identity. | Root grants, instance create, or flow writes. Label the mount as the root session until the clone is the session. |
| Tag routing | `oscal/` catalog and tag taxonomy, and the pure `catalog-routing` decision. | A live plugin call "because the router said allow." Enforcement through the mount is separate and is not wired. |
| Generated CMS | The generator (`json_render`: catalog, spec validation, generation) exists on the platform. | `cms/` has no app. `catalog-routing` `console_spec` is a grants console whose form submits nothing. Do not present either as the CMS. |

## Meta rules check

Checked 2026-10-31 against the public event page
<https://dev.meta.ai/events/global-hackathon> and the waiver scoring that
page's application terms describe. The event page still says Official Rules
are published before 26 October 2026 and that selected participants must
accept them. This check did not retrieve that PDF: a raw fetch of the page
returned 403. If that PDF adds a requirement, the PDF wins.

| Rule | Fit of this stage |
|---|---|
| Startup track. Judged on technical execution and whether it holds up in production. One project, one track. | The appliance is the production frame. The judged product is tag routing plus the generated CMS. Designated contact: Jeremy Hobson. |
| Submission 4 November 2026, 9:00 PM ET (02:00 UTC on 5 November). | A stage script does not meet the deadline. The working demo and the video are still required. |
| Impact, 30%. Who it helps, and whether it fits a theme. | A small firm uses a CMS whose actions are tagged and receipted. That fits "Build for Your World." The impact is the generated app, which is not ready. |
| Use of Meta AI tooling, 25%. Creative use of Meta's models, past a basic call. | The judged model step is Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3` at `https://api.meta.ai/v1`) writing the CMS spec. A hand-written spec does not score this. The chat router's Qwen model does not score this. A model-list call from this host on 2026-10-31 failed before any completion (`URLError`). Do not swap in another model. |
| Demo, 25%. A working demo, a live hold-up, and a demo video. | Not met. Rehearse the script only after each beat is proven. |
| Technical depth, 20%. Sound, finished engineering. | The depth is validation before render, tag decisions in code, and receipts from the appliance. The wiring between them is not ready. |
| Original work you own. Open source is allowed when the submission builds on it and keeps its licence. | New work is tag routing and the generated CMS. The appliance stays labeled pre-existing. |
| Secrets and training. | No keys, host addresses, or identity ids in the public repo or on a recorded screen. Use Standard mode for model calls. Contributor mode lets Meta train on prompts and outputs. |
| Submission licence. | Sending the project grants the organizers a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use it. Ownership stays with the entrant. Keep private client data out of the submission. |

## Rehearsal, once each beat is proven

1. One sentence: the appliance already existed; tag routing and this CMS are the new product.
2. One pre-tested call on the mount. Read back the operation id and the event hash. Say the session is still root.
3. One allowed tag route and one refusal. The refusal shows the rule and does not call a plugin.
4. One CMS spec that names Muse Spark, passes catalog validation, and renders. One publish shows the redaction notice and the receipt, or that action stays off the run.

If the model call fails, stop at beat 3. Do not play a recording of a different model. A recording counts only when that recording is a real Muse Spark generation.

No seal, no activation, no service restart, no grant change, no clone start,
and no retarget of the hackathon mount.

#!/bin/sh
# Prepare a single-user console and start a Cursor agent to finish the
# kernel-guard repair. Run this from sulogin after the runlevel is single.
#
#   sudo runsvchdir single
#   # sulogin on the console, then:

#
# The default runlevel is not restored. The agent must not create a subvolume,
# unload the guard, turn the guard off, or use an ordinary subvolume delete.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
umask 077

REPO=/srv/git/odbus-verified
EVIDENCE=/var/tmp/single-mode-finish
GUARD=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-storage/guardctl
AGENT=/home/jeremy/.local/bin/cursor-agent
PROMPT=$EVIDENCE/prompt.txt

die() { printf '%s\n' "single-mode-finish: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || die "run as root from the single-user console"
[ "$#" = 0 ] || die "takes no arguments"
runlevel=$(readlink -f /etc/runit/runsvdir/current 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$runlevel" = /etc/runit/runsvdir/single ] ||
    die "runlevel is ${runlevel:-unknown}; from a console run: runsvchdir single"

[ -x "$GUARD" ] || die "missing guardctl"
[ -x "$AGENT" ] || die "missing cursor-agent"
[ -d "$REPO" ] || die "missing repository"

mkdir -m 0700 -p "$EVIDENCE"
: > "$EVIDENCE/prepare.log"
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$*" | tee -a "$EVIDENCE/prepare.log"; }

log "recording guard and subvolume evidence"
{
    printf 'date %s\n' "$(date -Is)"
    printf 'uname %s\n' "$(uname -r)"
    printf 'runlevel %s\n' "$runlevel"
} > "$EVIDENCE/identity.txt"
"$GUARD" status > "$EVIDENCE/guard-status.txt" 2>&1 || true
btrfs subvolume list / > "$EVIDENCE/subvolumes.txt" 2>&1 || true
findmnt -A -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS > "$EVIDENCE/findmnt.txt" 2>&1 || true
awk '
    $0 ~ /subvolid=489/ || $0 ~ /@release-a/ || $0 ~ /release-640f40aa/ || $0 ~ /release-48d4b225/ {
        print
    }
' /proc/1/mountinfo > "$EVIDENCE/root-489-mounts.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
ip -br addr > "$EVIDENCE/addresses.txt" 2>&1 || true
ip route show > "$EVIDENCE/routes.txt" 2>&1 || true
for cgroup in opdbus-storage opdbus-release opdbus-incus; do
    printf '== %s\n' "$cgroup" >> "$EVIDENCE/cgroup-procs.txt"
    cat "/sys/fs/cgroup/$cgroup/cgroup.procs" >> "$EVIDENCE/cgroup-procs.txt" 2>&1 || true
done

if ! ip route show default | grep -q .; then
    log "no default route; the agent API call will fail until a route exists"
fi

if ! pgrep -x sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "starting sshd so this console is not the only way back"
    mkdir -p /run/sshd
    chmod 0755 /run/sshd
    /usr/sbin/sshd -t || die "sshd config test failed"
    /usr/sbin/sshd -E "$EVIDENCE/sshd.log"
fi

cat > "$PROMPT" <<'EOF'
Continue the kernel-guard repair from the single-user console. Read
/var/tmp/single-mode-finish/ and HANDOFF.md before changing anything.

The guard is loaded in GLOBAL mode and still failed two jobs: it allowed new
subvolumes (IDs 494, 495, 500, and top-level 501) and it did not enforce the
rule on existing subvolumes. Exact-generation checked-delete of root 489
(@release-a) returned EBUSY. Root 501 is not a release slot.

Finish only this:
- Find the live reference that keeps root 489 busy. Record it in the evidence directory.
- Release that reference. Do not use an ordinary btrfs subvolume delete, and do not call the quiescent-destroy ioctl by hand.
- After the census is zero, recover the interrupted release only through the installed op-release launcher.
- Close the hole that let a trusted cgroup create a new subvolume. Do not turn the guard off, unload it, or add a trust binding.
- Do not run runsvchdir default. Leave the host in single mode and write what the operator must run to return.

Do not create a subvolume. Do not delete any root other than what the launcher's own checked-delete already intends. Do not restart the application services.
EOF

log "launching cursor-agent as jeremy"
cd "$REPO"
exec runuser -u jeremy -- \
    env HOME=/home/jeremy USER=jeremy LOGNAME=jeremy \
        TERM="${TERM:-linux}" \
        PATH="/home/jeremy/.local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin" \
    "$AGENT" --force --sandbox disabled --cwd "$REPO" \
    "$(cat "$PROMPT")"

#!/bin/sh
# Finish the parked golden install once per boot, before application services
# can hold btrfs root 495.
#
#   install   early boot, from rcS, before the committed slot is mounted
#   activate  after runsvdir is up, switches the live slot to the received release
#
# The script never creates a subvolume, never uses an ordinary subvolume
# delete, never calls the quiescent-destroy ioctl itself, and never changes
# the kernel guard. A failure is recorded and boot continues.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
umask 077

LAUNCH=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch
EVIDENCE=/var/tmp/op-release-startup-finish
EXPECTED_ID=497
EXPECTED_NAME=release-f7c28383-9cc3-4081-929c-1047f8fecf1f

phase=${1:-}
[ "$phase" = install ] || [ "$phase" = activate ] || {
    printf '%s\n' 'usage: startup-finish.sh {install|activate}' >&2
    exit 2
}
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || {
    printf '%s\n' 'startup-finish.sh: root required' >&2
    exit 1
}

mkdir -m 0700 -p "$EVIDENCE"
log() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$*" | tee -a "$EVIDENCE/log"; }

status_file() { "$LAUNCH" status > "$EVIDENCE/status.json" 2>"$EVIDENCE/status.err"; }

json_get() {
    jq -r "$1" "$EVIDENCE/status.json" 2>/dev/null || true
}

ensure_release_cgroup() {
    [ "$(stat -f -c %T /sys/fs/cgroup 2>/dev/null || true)" = cgroup2fs ] || return 1
    cgroup=/sys/fs/cgroup/opdbus-release
    if [ ! -e "$cgroup" ] && [ ! -L "$cgroup" ]; then
        mkdir -m 0700 "$cgroup"
    fi
    [ -d "$cgroup" ] && [ ! -L "$cgroup" ] || return 1
    chown 0:0 "$cgroup"
    chmod 0700 "$cgroup"
    for control in cgroup.procs cgroup.threads cgroup.subtree_control; do
        [ -f "$cgroup/$control" ] && [ ! -L "$cgroup/$control" ] || return 1
        chown 0:0 "$cgroup/$control"
        chmod 0600 "$cgroup/$control"
    done
}

ensure_shm() {
    if [ ! -d /dev/shm/opdbus ]; then
        mkdir -m 0755 /dev/shm/opdbus
    fi
    chown 0:0 /dev/shm/opdbus
    chmod 0755 /dev/shm/opdbus
}

reassert_hackbr0() {
    command -v incus >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    addr=$(incus network get hackbr0 ipv4.address 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$addr" in
        ''|none) return 0 ;;
    esac
    log "hackbr0 had ${addr}; clearing it"
    incus network set hackbr0 ipv4.dhcp=false
    incus network set hackbr0 ipv4.nat=false
    incus network set hackbr0 ipv6.address=none
    incus network set hackbr0 ipv4.address=none
}

run_launch() {
    seconds=$1
    shift
    timeout -k 20 "$seconds" "$LAUNCH" "$@" > "$EVIDENCE/${phase}.out" 2>&1
}

if ! ensure_release_cgroup; then
    log "${phase}: release cgroup unavailable; nothing changed"
    exit 0
fi
if ! status_file; then
    log "${phase}: release status failed; nothing changed"
    exit 0
fi

operation=$(json_get '.state.journal.operation // ""')
step=$(json_get '.state.journal.step // ""')
active=$(json_get '.state.active // ""')
slot_b_id=$(json_get '.state.slots.b.id // ""')
slot_b_name=$(json_get '.state.slots.b.name // ""')

case "$phase" in
    install)
        if [ "$operation" != deploy ] || [ "$step" != "quiescent-delete:${EXPECTED_ID}" ]; then
            log "install: no parked delete of root ${EXPECTED_ID} (operation=${operation:-none} step=${step:-none})"
            exit 0
        fi
        ensure_shm
        log "install: resuming parked delete of root ${EXPECTED_ID}"
        set +e
        run_launch 180 release
        launch_rc=$?
        set -e
        status_file || true
        operation=$(json_get '.state.journal.operation // ""')
        slot_b_id=$(json_get '.state.slots.b.id // ""')
        slot_b_name=$(json_get '.state.slots.b.name // ""')
        if [ -z "$operation" ] && [ "$slot_b_id" = "$EXPECTED_ID" ] && [ "$slot_b_name" = "$EXPECTED_NAME" ]; then
            log "install: slot B is ${EXPECTED_NAME}; activate follows after services start"
            printf 'installed %s\n' "$(date -Is)" > "$EVIDENCE/installed"
        else
            log "install: root ${EXPECTED_ID} still blocked (launcher ${launch_rc}, journal ${operation:-none}, slot B ${slot_b_id:-none})"
        fi
        ;;
    activate)
        if [ -n "$operation" ]; then
            log "activate: journal ${operation} ${step} is still open; not switching slots"
            exit 0
        fi
        if [ "$active" = b ] && [ "$slot_b_name" = "$EXPECTED_NAME" ]; then
            log "activate: ${EXPECTED_NAME} is already live"
            reassert_hackbr0 || log "activate: hackbr0 check failed"
            exit 0
        fi
        if [ "$slot_b_id" != "$EXPECTED_ID" ] || [ "$slot_b_name" != "$EXPECTED_NAME" ]; then
            log "activate: slot B is ${slot_b_id:-none} ${slot_b_name:-none}; waiting for the early install"
            exit 0
        fi
        ensure_shm
        log "activate: switching the live slot to ${EXPECTED_NAME}"
        set +e
        run_launch 240 activate b
        launch_rc=$?
        set -e
        status_file || true
        active=$(json_get '.state.active // ""')
        slot_b_name=$(json_get '.state.slots.b.name // ""')
        if [ "$launch_rc" -eq 0 ] && [ "$active" = b ] && [ "$slot_b_name" = "$EXPECTED_NAME" ]; then
            log "activate: live slot is ${EXPECTED_NAME}"
            printf 'active %s %s\n' "$EXPECTED_NAME" "$(date -Is)" > "$EVIDENCE/receipt"
        else
            log "activate: switch failed (launcher ${launch_rc}, active ${active:-none})"
        fi
        i=0
        while [ "$i" -lt 30 ]; do
            if incus network get hackbr0 ipv4.address >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                break
            fi
            i=$((i + 1))
            sleep 1
        done
        reassert_hackbr0 || log "activate: hackbr0 check failed"
        ;;
esac
exit 0
